title: Their brother asked: will you not fear Allah?
subtitle: A warning from one of their own
then: Allah calls Nuh {reward}their brother{/reward}. He was one of them. His first words are a question: {idea}will you not have taqwa?{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it as: do you not fear Allah when you worship others instead of Him?
now: The warning that annoys you most often comes from your own sibling, your own friend, your own spouse. {reward}They say it because they are your people.{/reward} A brother's warning is love speaking.
old: When family criticizes me, it is because they do not understand me.
new: Sometimes the warning comes from family because they care the most.
try: Think of a sincere warning from someone close. Thank them for it.

title: I am a messenger you can trust.
subtitle: Nothing added, nothing taken away
then: Nuh says {idea}I am a trustworthy messenger to you.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: I convey the messages of my Lord {reward}and I do not add anything to them or take anything away.{/reward} His trust was in passing it on exactly.
now: Someone tells you a secret, a colleague asks you to pass a message, a friend shares a hadith in the group. {idea}Do you pass it on exactly, or add a little spin?{/idea} Being trustworthy is in the small relays too.
old: A little exaggeration when I pass something on is harmless.
new: Trust means passing things on exactly as they were given to me.
try: Next time you repeat what someone said, say it exactly, without adding anything.

title: Fear Allah, and follow me.
subtitle: Taqwa first, then following
then: Nuh puts it in order: {idea}have taqwa of Allah{/idea}, then obey me. He is not asking for a following of his own. Ibn Kathir says he is {reward}faithfully fulfilling the mission{/reward} Allah gave him, so following him means following Allah's message.
now: You follow a speaker online, a sheikh, a teacher you love. Good. {idea}Ask what the order is: do you follow them because they bring you to Allah, or for them?{/idea} Taqwa comes first.
old: Following a good teacher is enough on its own.
new: I follow teachers because they lead me to Allah. Allah comes first.
try: Next time you listen to a lesson, ask: what does Allah want me to do with this?

title: I am not asking you for anything.
subtitle: Advice with no price tag

row.title: what is in it for him?

then: Nuh says {idea}no reward do I ask of you for it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: I do not want any payment for the advice I give you; {reward}I will save my reward for it with Allah.{/reward} He had nothing to gain from them.
now: You help a friend move, check a cousin's CV, teach your neighbor's kid to read. You catch yourself waiting for thanks. {reward}Do it for Allah, and you will never be disappointed.{/reward} The pay comes from Him.
old: If I help someone, I deserve at least some thanks back.
new: When I help for Allah, my reward is already safe with Him.
try: Help someone today and do not mention it to anyone.

title: So fear Allah and obey me. He says it again.
subtitle: Repeating the call, with a new reason
then: Nuh repeats the same line. The first time it followed his trustworthiness. Now it follows the fact that he asks for nothing. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {idea}it is clear to you that I am telling the truth{/idea}, so fear Allah. {reward}He kept calling, with patience.{/reward}
now: You told your teenager once and gave up. You reminded your spouse gently once and stopped. {reward}Nuh repeated himself, gently, giving a new reason each time.{/reward} Some good things need to be said more than once.
old: If I said it once and it did not work, there is no point repeating it.
new: Patient, kind repetition is part of caring for someone.
try: Gently repeat one piece of good advice to someone you love, in a new way.

title: Believe you? Your followers are the lowest of us.
subtitle: Rejecting truth because of who accepted it
then: The leaders of Nuh's people said: we will not follow you and {trap}become equal to the meanest people{/trap} who follow you. Ibn Kathir notes they called them the lowest among us. The Prophet ﷺ heard the same from Quraysh: {trap}your followers are slaves and the poor.{/trap}
now: You skip the small masjid because the people there are not your type. You ignore good advice because it came from the cleaner, or the intern. {idea}The truth does not change with the clothes of the one who carries it.{/idea}
old: If the people accepting it are not impressive, it probably is not worth much.
new: The truth is true no matter who accepts it first.
try: Sit with or listen to someone today whom you would usually overlook.

title: What do I know about what they used to do?
subtitle: Not checking backgrounds at the door
then: Ibn Kathir explains Nuh's reply: {idea}what does it have to do with me if they follow me?{/idea} No matter what they did before, {reward}I do not have to check on them and examine their background.{/reward} All he had to do was accept them if they believed.
now: A brother with a prison record starts coming to the masjid. A new convert with tattoos joins the circle. People whisper about their past. {reward}Their past is not yours to investigate.{/reward} Welcome them.
old: Before I accept someone, I should know what they have done.
new: If someone turns to Allah, their past is not my business to dig into.
try: Greet one newcomer at your masjid or community warmly this week.

title: Their account is with my Lord, not with me.
subtitle: Leaving hearts to the One who knows them

row.title: mine
sub: I can tell who is sincere

then: Nuh continues: {idea}their account is only with my Lord, if you could but know.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}whatever is in their hearts is for Allah to know.{/reward} Nuh's task was the message, not judging the inner state of those who accepted it.
now: You decide someone's hijab is for show, someone's charity is for likes, someone's tears in prayer are fake. {idea}You cannot see inside them.{/idea} Their account is with Allah. Yours is too.
old: I can usually tell when someone's religion is fake.
new: Only Allah knows what is in a heart. I will leave the account to Him.
try: Catch one judgment about someone's sincerity today and let it go.

title: I will not push away the believers.
subtitle: Refusing to trade the poor for the powerful
then: Ibn Kathir says it seems the leaders {trap}asked him to drive these people away, and then they would follow him.{/trap} Nuh refused: {reward}I am not going to drive away the believers.{/reward} Whoever believes in me belongs to me and I to him, noble or common.
now: Your group wants to look good. Someone suggests not inviting the awkward guy so the important people come. {reward}Nuh would not trade one sincere person for a room full of the influential.{/reward}
old: It is worth leaving some people out to attract more important ones.
new: I will not push away sincere people to please the powerful.
try: Include someone in your next gathering who usually gets left out.

title: I am only a clear warner.
subtitle: Knowing the limits of your role
then: Nuh closes his answer: {idea}I am only a plain warner.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: I have been sent as a warner, and {reward}whoever believes in me belongs to me{/reward}, whether upper-class or lower-class. He does not decide who deserves the message.
now: You run the youth group, the study circle, the family WhatsApp. It is easy to start choosing who belongs. {idea}Your job is to share what is good, clearly and to everyone.{/idea} Not to guard the door.
old: Part of my role is deciding who deserves to hear this.
new: My role is to share clearly. Who accepts it is not mine to sort.
try: Share one good reminder today with someone you would not usually share it with.

title: Stop, Nuh, or we will stone you.
subtitle: After years of calling, a death threat
then: Ibn Kathir says Nuh {idea}stayed among his people a long time, calling them night and day, in secret and openly.{/idea} The more he called, the more they clung to disbelief. In the end they said: {trap}if you do not stop, we will stone you.{/trap}
now: You have been patient for years with a family member, a difficult coworker, a friend. It only got worse. {idea}Sometimes your patience is not failing. You did your part, like Nuh.{/idea} Their hardness is theirs.
old: If they only got worse, I must have done it wrong.
new: I can call with patience for years and still not be the cause of their refusal.
try: Tell Allah about one long effort that has not worked. Ask Him for strength.

title: My Lord, my people have called me a liar.
subtitle: Bringing the pain straight to Allah
then: When the threat came, Nuh turned to Allah: {idea}My Lord, my people have denied me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says Allah responded to his prayer, and compares it to another verse where Nuh says {trap}I have been overcome, so help me.{/trap}
now: You were not believed. The family took the other side, the manager did not back you. You want to post about it, call everyone. {idea}Nuh took it to his Lord first.{/idea} Tell Him exactly what happened.
old: When I am hurt, I need everyone to know what they did.
new: My deepest complaints are best brought to Allah first.
try: Next time you feel wronged, pray and tell Allah before telling anyone else.

title: Judge between us, and save me and the believers.
subtitle: Handing the outcome to Allah
then: Nuh asks Allah to {idea}judge between me and them with a decisive judgement{/idea}, and to {reward}save me and the believers with me.{/reward} He did not take matters into his own hands. He asked Allah to decide, and remembered those who believed with him.
now: There is a conflict you cannot resolve, with an ex, a business partner, a sibling. You fantasize about getting even. {idea}Hand it to Allah: judge between us.{/idea} And remember to pray for the people on your side.
old: If I do not settle this myself, it will never be fair.
new: I can hand the judgment to Allah and ask Him to protect the good people with me.
try: Make a dua for justice in one conflict, and include the people who stood by you.

title: Saved in a ship packed full.
subtitle: Nuh and those with him are rescued
then: Allah says {reward}We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says the laden ship was {idea}filled with cargo and the couples, one pair from every species.{/idea} The followers the elite called the lowest were the ones on board.
now: The people others looked down on, the quiet family next door, the ones who did not make it to the top of the company. {reward}Allah's rescue is not sorted by status.{/reward} Be with the believers, whoever they are.
old: The safe place is with the popular and powerful.
new: Safety is with the believers, however lowly others think they are.
try: Make a dua today for one humble believer you know.

title: Then the rest were drowned.
subtitle: The end of those who refused Nuh
then: Allah says {trap}then We drowned the rest thereafter.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: We saved Nuh and all who followed him, and drowned all those who disbelieved in him and went against his commands. {idea}For years the door was open. Then the ship sailed.{/idea}
now: You keep saying you will fix it later: the prayer, the apology, the debt you owe. {idea}Every door that is open now will close one day.{/idea} The ship is still at the dock. Get on.
old: There will always be more time to turn back.
new: The chance is open now, but not forever. Today is the day to board.
try: Do the one thing today you keep telling yourself you will do later.
